name: Security Incident
description: A broad category of security events including cyberattacks, data breaches, unauthorized access, and system failures. The primary objective for these incidents is to minimize impact and restore operations quickly.
context: procedures for detecting, investigating, and responding to security incidents (cyberattacks, data breaches, unauthorized access, system failures)

name: Security Incident Detection
description: The initial phase of the security incident response process focused on identifying the occurrence of a security event.
context: procedures for detecting, investigating, and responding to security incidents

name: Security Incident Investigation
description: The process of analyzing a detected security incident to determine its scope, cause, and impact.
context: procedures for detecting, investigating, and responding to security incidents

name: Security Incident Response
description: The active phase of managing a security incident to minimize impact and restore operational stability.
context: procedures for detecting, investigating, and responding to security incidents

name: Cybersecurity Incident
description: A category of operational incidents involving digital security threats, including malware, ransomware, unauthorized access, data exfiltration, DDoS attacks, and credential compromise.

name: Data Breach
description: An incident where sensitive information is exposed or accessed without authorization, specifically covering customer personal data, financial data, system/operational data, or regulatory data.

name: System Incident
description: Operational failures related to technical infrastructure, including total system outages, data corruption, performance degradation, integration failures, and backup failures.

name: Physical Security Incident
description: Incidents involving the physical security of bank assets and facilities, such as facility breaches, equipment theft, environmental damage (fire), and access control failures.

name: Fraud/Misconduct
description: Incidents involving fraudulent activity or misconduct, encompassing unauthorized transactions as well as fraud perpetrated by employees or third parties.

name: Severity 1 (Critical) — >£100,000 impact or >4-hour system outage
description: The highest severity tier characterized by major data breaches affecting over 1,000 customers, ransomware on critical systems, or system outages exceeding 4 hours. It involves significant regulatory violations and an estimated financial impact greater than £100,000.
context: Major data breach (personal data exposed, >1,000 customers)

name: Severity 2 (High) — £10,000–£100,000 impact or 1–4 hour system outage
description: A high severity tier involving suspected data breaches affecting fewer than 1,000 customers, unauthorized access, or system outages between 1 and 4 hours. Financial impact is estimated between £10,000 and £100,000, and may include fraud incidents over £10,000.

name: Severity 3 (Medium) — £1,000–£10,000 impact
description: A medium severity tier covering unconfirmed unauthorized access, contained malware, or system performance issues. It includes fraud incidents under £10,000 and policy violations, with an estimated financial impact between £1,000 and £10,000.

name: Severity 4 (Low) — <£1,000 impact
description: The lowest severity tier for minor incidents such as false positive security alerts, minor policy violations, or system hiccups with minimal impact. The estimated financial impact is less than £1,000.

name: Data Breach
description: An incident involving the exposure of personal customer data. It is classified as Severity 1 if more than 1,000 customers are affected and Severity 2 if fewer than 1,000 are affected.
context: Major data breach (personal data exposed, >1,000 customers)

name: Ransomware
description: A cybersecurity incident where ransomware affects critical systems, automatically triggering a Severity 1 classification.

name: System Outage
description: A failure of system availability. Outages exceeding 4 hours are Severity 1, while those between 1 and 4 hours are Severity 2, and minor hiccups are Severity 4.

name: Unauthorized Access
description: Incidents involving unauthorized entry into systems. Confirmed detection is Severity 2, while suspected but unconfirmed access is Severity 3.

name: Fraud Incident
description: Fraud events categorized by financial impact: those over £10,000 are Severity 2, and those under £10,000 are Severity 3.

name: Regulatory Violation
description: Incidents involving breaches of regulatory requirements. Significant violations are Severity 1, while general regulatory concerns are Severity 2.

name: Malware Detection
description: The detection of malicious software. When the malware is contained, it is classified as a Severity 3 incident.

name: Policy Violation
description: Breaches of internal bank policy. General violations are Severity 3, while minor violations are Severity 4.

name: System Performance Issue
description: Issues relating to the speed or efficiency of systems, classified as Severity 3.

name: Incident Commander (IC)
description: The primary authority responsible for directing the incident response and making critical decisions. The role is primarily held by the Chief Information Security Officer, with the Chief Technology Officer serving as backup.

name: Chief Information Security Officer
description: The primary individual designated as the Incident Commander (IC) with authority to direct response and make decisions.

name: Chief Technology Officer
description: The backup individual designated as the Incident Commander (IC) to direct response and make decisions.

name: Technology Lead
description: A member of the Response Team providing system expertise during an incident.

name: Security Lead
description: A member of the Response Team responsible for the investigation phase of an incident.

name: Communications Lead
description: A member of the Response Team responsible for managing both internal and external messaging.

name: Operations Lead
description: A member of the Response Team focused on the restoration of services.

name: Compliance/Legal
description: A member of the Response Team ensuring that regulatory obligations are met during an incident.

name: Severity 1 — Immediate escalation (within 1 hour)
description: The highest severity level requiring immediate escalation to the on-call rotation within a 1-hour timeframe.

name: Severity 2 — Escalation within 2 hours
description: A high severity level requiring escalation to the on-call rotation within 2 hours.

name: Severity 3 — Next business day escalation
description: A medium severity level where escalation to the on-call rotation is required by the next business day.

name: Severity 4 — Logged, scheduled investigation
description: The lowest severity level where the event is logged and a scheduled investigation is performed.

name: Immediate Escalation
description: The process of escalating an incident to the on-call rotation based on the assigned severity level.

name: Detect & Alert Phase
description: The initial phase of the Incident Response Procedure occurring within 0–15 minutes. It encompasses detection methods, immediate verification, classification, and the activation of the response team.
context: Detection Methods: Automated alerts (SIEM, IDS, monitoring), Staff report (customer, employee, system), Regulatory notification (law enforcement, regulator), Third-party notification (vendor, partner)

name: Report Action
description: The immediate action where an alert reaches the on-call incident commander to initiate the response process.
context: 1. Report: Alert reaches on-call incident commander

name: Verify Action
description: The process of confirming that a reported incident is a real event and not a false alarm.
context: 2. Verify: Confirm incident is real (not false alarm)

name: Classify Action
description: The step of assigning a severity level from 1 to 4 to the identified incident.

name: Notify Action
description: The action of escalating the incident according to the defined escalation matrix.

name: Activate Action
description: The final step of the detection phase involving the convening of the incident response team.

name: Severity 1 (Critical)
description: The highest severity level requiring immediate notification of the Executive team and notification of the Board within 2 hours.

name: Severity 2 (High)
description: A high severity level requiring Executive team notification within 30 minutes and CRO notification within 1 hour.
context: Severity 2: Executive team (within 30 min), CRO (within 1 hour)

name: Severity 3 (Medium)
description: A medium severity level requiring notification of the Department head within 4 hours.

name: Severity 4 (Low)
description: The lowest severity level where the required action is to log the incident as routine.

name: Executive Team
description: Internal leadership team to be notified ASAP for Severity 1 incidents and within 30 minutes for Severity 2 incidents.

name: Board
description: The governing board to be notified within 2 hours for Severity 1 incidents.

name: Chief Risk Officer (CRO)
description: The CRO to be notified within 1 hour for Severity 2 incidents.

name: Department Head
description: The relevant department head to be notified within 4 hours for Severity 3 incidents.

name: Law Enforcement
description: External regulatory body that may provide notifications to trigger the detection phase.

name: Regulator
description: External regulatory body that may provide notifications to trigger the detection phase.

name: Third-party Vendor/Partner
description: External partners or vendors that may provide notifications to trigger the detection phase.

name: Containment Phase
description: The second phase of incident response occurring between 15–60 minutes. The primary objectives are to stop the attack or prevent spread, preserve evidence, protect unaffected systems, and maintain business continuity.
context: Objectives: Stop attack/prevent spread, Preserve evidence, Protect unaffected systems, Maintain business continuity

name: Cyberattack (Malware/Ransomware)
description: A security incident involving malware or ransomware that requires immediate system isolation, credential resets, and IP blocking to prevent further spread.
context: Prevent further access (reset credentials, block IP)

name: Isolate Affected System
description: A containment action for cyberattacks involving the disconnection of the affected system from the network to stop the spread of malware or ransomware.

name: Prevent Further Access
description: A containment action for cyberattacks involving the resetting of credentials and blocking of IP addresses to stop unauthorized access.
context: Prevent further access (reset credentials, block IP)

name: Preserve Logs and Evidence
description: The process of copying logs and evidence before system shutdown to ensure a forensic trail is maintained during a cyberattack or data breach.

name: Kill Processes
description: An action to terminate active malicious processes, provided it can be done without causing data loss.
context: Kill processes (if possible without data loss)

name: Data Breach
description: An incident involving the compromise of data, requiring the identification of scope, revocation of credentials, and monitoring for misuse of PII.

name: Identify Compromised Data Scope
description: The process of determining the specific scope and nature of the data compromised during a data breach.

name: Monitor for Misuse
description: Ongoing monitoring for the misuse of Personally Identifiable Information (PII), which may include implementing credit monitoring.
context: Monitor for misuse (credit monitoring if PII)

name: System Outage
description: An operational failure resulting in system unavailability, requiring failover to backups and isolation of failed components.

name: Failover to Backup
description: The action of switching operations to a backup system when the primary system suffers an outage.

name: Isolate Failed Component
description: The process of separating a malfunctioning system component to prevent the outage from escalating.

name: Fraud
description: An incident involving fraudulent activity that requires freezing compromised accounts and blocking unauthorized transactions.

name: Freeze Compromised Account
description: An immediate action to lock a customer account suspected of being compromised to prevent further fraud.

name: Block Fraudulent Transactions
description: The action of stopping specific unauthorized financial transactions from being processed.

name: Investigation Phase
description: The third phase of the incident response process occurring between 1 and 24 hours. It focuses on determining the incident timeline, scope, root cause, data impact, threat actor, and evidence collection.

name: Evidence Preservation
description: A critical operational step within the investigation phase to ensure the integrity of data. This includes maintaining the chain of custody, protecting collected logs, taking system snapshots, and establishing a timeline.

name: Recovery & Restoration Phase
description: The fourth phase of the incident response process occurring between 1 and 48 hours. It encompasses system recovery, data recovery, and service restoration activities.

name: Backup Restore
description: A system recovery action requiring the restoration of systems from a clean backup to ensure a known good state.
context: Backup Restore: Restore from clean backup

name: Security Patch Application
description: The process of applying security patches during the system recovery phase to prevent re-infection or further vulnerability.

name: System Rebuild
description: The action of rebuilding systems from clean media if standard backup restoration is insufficient or unavailable.
context: Rebuild: Rebuild from clean media (if needed)

name: Functionality and Malware Verification
description: A testing step to verify that system functionality is restored and that no malware remains in the environment.

name: Re-infection Monitoring
description: Continuous observation of systems following recovery to detect any signs of re-infection.

name: Data Recovery Identification
description: The initial step of data recovery focused on identifying exactly what data requires recovery.

name: Data Backup Restoration
description: The process of restoring identified data from backups.

name: Data Integrity Validation
description: The process of verifying that restored data is accurate and has maintained its integrity.

name: Customer Breach Notification
description: The action of notifying customers specifically in the event that a data breach has occurred.

name: Phased Service Restoration
description: A strategic approach to service restoration where critical services are brought back online first.

name: Pre-Restoration Verification
description: Testing services to ensure they are stable before proceeding to full restoration.

name: Capacity Validation
description: Ensuring that restored systems are capable of handling normal operational loads.
context: Capacity: Ensure systems handle normal load

name: Post-Incident Enhanced Monitoring
description: The implementation of heightened monitoring levels immediately following the restoration of services.

name: Customers
description: Bank customers who must be notified if a data breach is identified during the data recovery process.

name: Notify & Report Phase
description: The fifth phase of the incident response process, occurring between 24 and 72 hours post-incident, focused on notification and reporting requirements.

name: Executive Team (CEO, CFO, CRO)
description: The senior leadership team consisting of the CEO, CFO, and CRO who must be notified immediately within 4 hours of an event.

name: Board of Directors
description: The governing Board, required to be notified immediately (within 4 hours) specifically for incidents classified as Severity 1 or 2.

name: Department Heads of Affected Areas
description: Leaders of the specific business areas impacted by the incident, requiring immediate notification within 4 hours.

name: All Staff
description: The general employee population to be notified via email and meeting within a 24-hour follow-up window.

name: Affected Customers
description: Bank customers who must be notified within 24 hours specifically in the event of a data breach.

name: Affected Partners and Vendors
description: External third-party partners or vendors who are impacted by the incident, requiring notification within 24 hours.

name: Immediate Internal Notification
description: The initial notification phase requiring communication to the Executive team, Board, and Department heads within a 4-hour window.

name: Follow-up Internal and External Notification
description: The secondary notification phase occurring within 24 hours, targeting all staff, customers (in case of data breach), and affected partners.

name: Data Breach
description: A security event involving unauthorized access to data that triggers a mandatory customer notification within 24 hours.

name: Regulatory Notification
description: The process of notifying external regulatory bodies based on the nature of the breach or incident, with specific timeframes for the ICO and FCA.

name: Information Commissioner's Office (ICO)
description: The regulatory body that must be notified within 72 hours in the event of a Data Breach involving personal data.
context: Data Breach (Personal Data): ICO within 72 hours

name: Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)
description: The regulatory body that must be notified within 24 hours in the event of a suspected security breach.

name: Law Enforcement
description: The external party to be contacted via a police report in cases of fraud or crime.

name: Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI)
description: The regulatory body to be notified if a sanctions violation occurs.

name: Customer Notification
description: The procedure for notifying affected customers of a data breach via email or letter within 72 hours, including incident details and mitigation support.
context: Content: Incident description, impact, mitigation, contact info

name: Affected Customer
description: The bank customer who must be notified within 72 hours of a data breach and may be offered credit monitoring.

name: Data Breach (Personal Data)
description: An incident involving the compromise of personal data requiring notification to the ICO and affected customers within 72 hours.
context: Data Breach (Personal Data): ICO within 72 hours

name: Security Breach (Suspected)
description: A suspected security event that triggers a mandatory notification to the FCA within 24 hours.

name: Fraud/Crime
description: Incidents categorized as fraud or crime that require the filing of a police report with law enforcement.

name: Sanctions Breach
description: An incident involving a violation of sanctions requiring notification to OFSI.

name: Incident Report Documentation
description: The formal process of documenting an incident, which must include a summary, timeline, root cause analysis, impact assessment, remediation steps, and prevention recommendations.

name: Executive Team
description: Internal leadership group designated to receive the distribution of the Incident Report.

name: Board Risk Committee
description: Governance body responsible for risk oversight that must be included in the Incident Report distribution.

name: Internal Audit
description: Internal oversight function designated to receive the distribution of the Incident Report.

name: Regulators
description: External regulatory bodies that must be notified and provided with the Incident Report if required by compliance or law.

name: Post-Incident Review
description: A formal review phase occurring 1–2 weeks after an incident to discuss lessons learned, root causes, and preventive actions. It involves the incident commander, response team, and key stakeholders.

name: Root Cause Analysis
description: A specific review topic focused on identifying the technical and process-related reasons why an incident occurred.
context: Why Did It Happen? Root cause (technical and process)

name: Preventive and Corrective Action Planning
description: The process of determining the necessary fixes to prevent recurrence, assigning owners, and establishing a completion timeline.
context: What's Our Fix? Preventive and corrective actions

name: Corrective Action Implementation and Verification
description: The follow-up phase where assigned owners implement fixes within 30–90 days and effectiveness is verified via audit or re-testing.

name: Incident Commander
description: The individual responsible for leading the Post-Incident Review meeting.

name: Incident Response Team
description: The team required to attend the Post-Incident Review meeting.

name: Key Stakeholders
description: Relevant internal parties included in the Post-Incident Review process.

name: Severity 1 (Critical) — Hourly updates to executive team
description: The highest severity level requiring the most frequent internal communication cadence, specifically hourly updates to the executive team.
context: Severity 1: Hourly updates to executive team

name: Severity 2 (High) — 2-hourly updates
description: A high severity level requiring internal communication updates every two hours.

name: Severity 3 (Medium) — Daily updates
description: A medium severity level requiring internal communication updates on a daily basis.

name: Severity 4 (Low) — Email summary
description: The lowest severity level where internal communication is handled via an email summary.

name: Executive Team
description: The internal leadership group that must receive hourly updates during Severity 1 incidents.

name: Internal Communication
description: The process of providing status updates during an incident, utilizing a specific template including Time, Status, Impact, Actions, ETA, and Next Update.
context:
Time: [HH:MM]
Status: [Ongoing / Controlled / Resolved]
Impact: [Description of customer/system impact]
Actions: [What we're doing]
ETA: [Estimated restoration time]
Next Update: [When next communication]

name: Data Breach
description: A specific category of operational incident involving the unauthorized access or disclosure of customer data, requiring a structured communication response including incident description and mitigation details.

name: Customer Communication for Data Breach
description: The process of notifying affected customers via email or letter following a data breach. The communication must include the incident description, timeline, affected data, mitigation steps, required customer actions, support options, and an apology.
context: Data affected (type, scope, number of customers)
Support (credit monitoring, phone line for questions)

name: Affected Customers
description: The recipients of breach notifications, specifically those whose data has been affected in terms of type, scope, and number.
context: Data affected (type, scope, number of customers)

name: Affected Customer
description: Customers who have had their data compromised during a data breach and are the targets of mandatory communication and support efforts.
context: Data affected (type, scope, number of customers)

name: Ransomware
description: A cybersecurity incident involving ransomware that affects critical banking infrastructure, specifically the payment processing system, leading to transaction failures and delayed customer funds.

name: Severity 1 (Critical) — >£50,000 impact or 4-hour outage
description: The highest severity tier triggered by a 4-hour outage, 100+ failed transactions, delayed customer funds, or an estimated financial impact exceeding £50,000. Requires immediate response and strict notification timelines.

name: Immediate Response
description: The required response urgency for Severity 1 incidents, necessitating an immediate start to mitigation and recovery efforts.

name: The Board
description: Internal executive body that must be notified within 2 hours of a Severity 1 incident occurring.

name: Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)
description: The external regulatory body that must be notified within 24 hours of a Severity 1 incident.

name: Regulatory Notification
description: The mandatory process of informing the FCA within a 24-hour window following a Severity 1 incident.

name: Board Notification
description: The mandatory process of escalating a Severity 1 incident to the Board within 2 hours.

name: Payment Processing System
description: The core banking system responsible for processing payments, identified as the affected system in the Severity 1 ransomware scenario.

name: Failed Transactions
description: Financial transactions that fail to process during a Severity 1 incident; a threshold of 100+ failed transactions defines this severity level.

name: Severity 2 — £10,000–£100,000 estimated investigation cost
description: A severity tier characterized by unauthorized access to customer data affecting approximately 50 customers, with investigation costs estimated between £10,000 and £100,000. Requires a response within 2 hours.

name: Unauthorized access to customer data
description: An operational incident involving the unauthorized access of personal data belonging to customers, specifically exemplified by a scenario where 50 customers' data was accessed without evidence of exfiltration.

name: Incident Response (Severity 2)
description: The required response action for a Severity 2 incident, which must be initiated within 2 hours of detection.

name: Executive Team
description: Internal executive leadership required to be notified during a Severity 2 unauthorized data access incident.

name: Chief Risk Officer (CRO)
description: The Chief Risk Officer is a mandatory notification contact for Severity 2 incidents involving unauthorized customer data access.

name: Regulator
description: External regulatory body whose notification status is subject to assessment following a Severity 2 data access incident.

name: Affected Customers
description: Customers whose personal data has been subject to unauthorized access, specifically 50 individuals in the provided example.

name: Malware detected on staff laptop
description: A routine security incident involving malware detection on a staff laptop, typically triggered by a user clicking a phishing link, where the threat is contained to a single endpoint.

name: Severity 3 — Routine incident
description: A medium-tier severity level for routine incidents where malware is contained to a single endpoint with no spread to other systems, requiring response by the next business day.

name: Endpoint Isolation
description: The action of isolating the affected endpoint to ensure malware is contained and does not spread to other systems.

name: Department Head
description: The internal management contact required to be notified for Severity 3 routine malware incidents.

name: Detection
description: The initial phase of incident response utilizing a suite of monitoring tools including SIEM (Splunk), IDS (Snort), Antivirus (EDR), and Log aggregation (ELK) to identify security events.

name: Investigation
description: The analytical phase of incident response employing forensic tools such as EnCase, WinDbg for memory dumps, Wireshark for packet analysis, and Autopsy for timeline reconstruction.

name: Communication
description: The process of disseminating information during an incident via a dedicated Incident Slack channel for real-time updates, a War room for major incidents, and email for external parties.
context: War room (video call, during major incidents)

name: Incident Slack Channel
description: An internal communication channel used for providing real-time updates during the course of an incident.

name: War Room
description: A video call environment convened specifically for the coordination and management of major incidents.
context: War room (video call, during major incidents)

name: Incident response procedures training
description: Annual training on incident response procedures mandatory for all IT staff to ensure operational readiness.

name: Forensic investigation training
description: Specialised annual training in forensic investigation specifically for the security team.

name: Breach notification training
description: Annual training on breach notification requirements conducted for the compliance team.

name: Annual Tabletop Exercise
description: A yearly simulation exercise designed to test response team activation, decision-making under pressure, and communication practices using simulated incident scenarios.

name: IT Staff
description: Internal technical personnel required to undergo annual incident response procedure training.

name: Security Team
description: Internal security personnel responsible for forensic investigation training.

name: Compliance Team
description: Internal compliance personnel responsible for breach notification training.
